description: Rents a whole GPU with SSH (and JupyterLab where its host serves it), paid in blocks of 15 minutes: gpu (an id from compute_catalog, or auto with vram), mode (auto or cheapest, fastest, secure), minutes and ssh_key (your OpenSSH public key, one line). Some GPUs are rented for 30 minutes at least, 20 of which are charged even if stopped sooner: the catalog gives each one’s minMinutes and chargedMinutes. Pay by signing one USDG transferWithAuthorization (EIP-3009) for exactly the amount and payee the payment request names, and send the same call again with it in _meta["x402/payment"] (MCP) or the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header (HTTP). No gas: this site settles it. The clock starts when the GPU is up, and the rental stops at the end of its paid time unless extended: call it again with rental_id, token and minutes to pay for more. If the GPU does not start, the payment goes back automatically. Returns the rental id and its token (keep it private: it shows the connection and stops the rental), then the SSH address (and Jupyter link) through compute_status. The GPU’s disk is wiped when the rental ends.

gpu.description: A GPU id from compute_catalog, or auto (default) to pick by vram and mode.

minutes.description: How long, in blocks of 15 minutes (default 60).

mode.description: auto or cheapest (the lowest rate), fastest (the quickest GPU that fits), secure (secure data centres only).

rental_id.description: To pay for more time on a rental.

ssh_key.description: Your OpenSSH public key, one line (a new rental).

vram.description: The least VRAM wanted, in GB (with gpu auto; default 16).

name: compute_rent
title: Rent a GPU (paid)
